about: Land suitability thresholds: can a field be cropped at all. Every value carries a source and 'verified'. verified:true is allowed only for a value with a cited source, or for an MVP default the owner approved (then mvpDefault:true: the number has no source and must be refined). Conditions only; the check never says which crop. 'unsuitable' stops crop recommendations for the field until an agronomist overrides it; 'limited' only warns; 'unknown' never blocks. Land capability class (LCC) is the US NRCS system, classes I-VIII. Not yet reviewed by the owner: every value is verified:false; sourced values cite their source, unsourced values are marked mvpDefault.

source.title: National Soil Survey Handbook, Part 622 (Interpretive Groups): land capability classification
source.note: Classes I-IV are suited to cultivation; classes V-VIII (V: wetness, flooding, stoniness; VI-VII: steep or shallow, pasture / forest; VIII: recreation, wildlife, water supply) are not suited to cultivated crops.

source.title: National Soil Survey Handbook, Part 622 (Interpretive Groups): land capability classification
source.note: Share of the outline in class V-VIII at or above which the whole field is unsuitable (area-weighted over map units).

source.note: Built area, water, flooded vegetation, trees and bare ground together (average of the latest seasons; US fields use the USDA Cropland Data Layer's developed, water, wetland, forest and barren classes). Rangeland and crops do not count.
